## Claims
- [source-backed] For every bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), and \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is minimally generated by \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- [computed] For \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), \(J=\bigoplus_{333\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^5}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda\), and \(Q=J/A_+J\), the ranks in weights \(9,\ldots,25\) are \((1,1,2,2,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)\), and every torsion list is empty. [artifact b5658ec18b84ad470751544a752f238dadd447fb7b1122a89a299a79e024042f]
- [proved] If a homogeneous family \(F\) generates a graded \(A\)-module \(J\), and every \(Q_d=(J/A_+J)_d\) is torsion-free with \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Q_d=\#F_d\), then the images of \(F_d\) form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q_d\).
- [proved] For \(i=j=b=3\), \(a=2\), the lower-adjoined family has degree enumerator
  \[
  z^9\!\!\sum_{\rho\subseteq3^2}z^{|\rho|}
  =z^9(1+z+2z^2+2z^3+2z^4+z^5+z^6)
  =z^9\binom52_z.
  \]
- [proved] Minimality alone does not imply the indecomposables-basis criterion: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(A_+=(x)\), and \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the homogeneous generators \(2x,x^2\) are minimal, whereas
  \[
  J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\{2x\}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)\{x^2\}.
  \]

## Strategy
Let \(F=\{\bar s_{(3,3,3,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq3^2\}\). The partitions \(\rho\subseteq3^2\), by weight, are
\[
\varnothing;\ (1);\ (2),(1,1);\ (3),(2,1);\ (3,1),(2,2);\ (3,2);\ (3,3),
\]
giving the displayed enumerator and degree counts \(1,1,2,2,2,1,1\).

Generation of \(F\) is source-backed. The computed torsion-free rank table therefore satisfies the single basis criterion: the degreewise surjection \(\mathbb Z^{\#F_d}\twoheadrightarrow Q_d\) has kernel of rank \(0\); as a subgroup of a free abelian group, it is free, hence zero. Thus \(F_d\) is a basis of \(Q_d\). Since \(J_d=0\) for \(d<9\) and \(d>25\),
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}_Q(z)=z^9\binom52_z
\]
for this interval only.

For the obstruction, \(A_+J=(2x^2,x^3)\). Neither \(2x\in(x^2)\) nor \(x^2\in(2x)\), so the pair is minimal; the displayed torsion prevents a basis conclusion.

**The requested strategy-pivot target is established via the single indecomposables-basis criterion; the original finite Hilbert-series target remains established only for \([333,5^5]\), while the proposed universal inference from minimality is not established.**

## Gaps
The finite computation does not establish torsion-freeness, the Hilbert series, or the basis criterion’s hypotheses for arbitrary parameters. The counterexample only rules out deriving those hypotheses from abstract minimality alone.
